drawdown_context: WOLF FY24 10-K (filed 2024-08-22) shows revenue of $807.2M, operating loss of $445.3M, net cash used in operations of $671.3M, and $6.16B long-term debt against $2.17B cash/STI — but management asserts 'adequate liquidity and capital resources to fund our operations for at least the next 12 months' with no going-concern language. A subsequent 10-Q filed 2025-05-09 (6 days pre-cutoff, for Q3 FY25 ending March 30 2025) explicitly discloses 'substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern' and management's 'ongoing consideration of an in-court restructuring that would result in an event of default.' The disclosure delta between Aug 2024 and May 2025 is the dispositive fact.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K (Aug 2024): 'Although we believe we have adequate liquidity and capital resources to fund our operations for at least the next 12 months, we expect to need additional funding to fully complete all of our intended expansion initiatives.' No going-concern or substantial-doubt language anywhere in the 10-K.
rfm_tuples.f: going_concern_local.going_concern_from_text on the FY24 10-K AND on the most-recent-pre-cutoff 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09); Mode B: did the next periodic filing reverse the assertion?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: signal=NO_GOING_CONCERN, n_matches=0. 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09): signal=EXPLICIT_GOING_CONCERN, n_matches=6, n_current_period=6. 10-Q sample: 'due to the Company's ongoing consideration of an in-court restructuring that would result in an event of default during the implementation of that potential solution, management has concluded that there is substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern as of the issuance date, in accordance with ASC 205-40.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The FY24 10-K's 'adequate liquidity for next 12 months' representation was reversed by management's own pen 8.6 months later, before that 12-month horizon expired. The 10-Q discloses BOTH substantial-doubt language AND explicit consideration of an in-court (Chapter 11) restructuring — the most severe disclosure tier in the framework, captured pre-cutoff.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'we have outstanding debt which could materially restrict our business' followed by debt schedule: $575M 2026 Notes (1.75% conv., due May 2026), $750M 2028 Notes, $1,750M 2029 Notes, $1,250M 2030 Senior Notes, plus $2.0B Renesas CRD deposits — total ~$6.3B at June 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on 10-K debt schedule + 10-Q debt note to verify maturity ladder and covenant headroom; Mode B: is the $575M 2026 Note maturity inside the 12-month liquidity window the 10-Q must cover?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q discloses $6.5B debt obligations at March 30, 2025 vs $6.16B at June 30, 2024. 10-Q: 'scheduled debt repayments and debt service costs of $575 million and $322 million, respectively, over the next 12 months' against $1,329.6M unrestricted cash — i.e. the $575M 2026 convertible maturity (May 2026) sits inside the 12-month going-concern horizon and consumes 43% of available liquidity before any operating burn (operating cash burn of $469M over the 9 months ended March 30 2025).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Debt grew $350M during a period of accelerating operating losses, while cash fell from $2.17B to $1.33B. The 2026 Note maturity falls inside the going-concern horizon and is mathematically incompatible with continued operations absent refinancing — which the 10-Q says they cannot achieve out-of-court.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: Mohawk Valley Fab 'began revenue production in late fiscal 2023... we expect to invest approximately $2.0 billion in total construction, equipment and other related costs for the new facility, of which approximately $500 million is expected to be reimbursed' — narrative of orderly ramp with $124.4M FY24 underutilization charge described as transitory ramp cost.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on 10-Q to measure whether MV utilization improved YoY (per 10-K narrative the ramp should be progressing); Mode B: did underutilization charges decrease as ramp progressed?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q (Q3 FY25): underutilization charges $26.3M (3mo) and $81.6M (9mo) at Mohawk Valley vs $30.4M / $100.4M same period prior year. Modest 13% YoY decrease in Q3 underutilization; ramp visibly slow given total FY24 charge was $124M. Revenue Q3 FY25 = $185.4M vs Q3 FY24 = $200.7M — revenue DOWN 8% YoY despite the MV ramp narrative. 10-Q: 'design-wins and design-ins decreased for the nine months ended March 30, 2025... customers begin to ramp previously reported design-ins, although at a lower ramp rate than initially expected.'
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 10-K framed MV underutilization as a temporary ramp burden; 10-Q confirms the ramp curve is materially slower than disclosed — revenue actually shrank YoY and management euphemistically acknowledges 'lower ramp rate than initially expected.' Not lying outright, but the 'ramp is on track' framing in the 10-K was optimistic.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'finalize negotiations on a Preliminary Memorandum of Terms and, if an agreement can be reached, complete comprehensive due diligence, finalize award documentation, and fulfill all conditions and milestones for and receive the expected benefits from capital grants through the CHIPS Act' — i.e. CHIPS Act grant funding contingent on award docs not yet executed. Company had already booked $641.8M property-and-equipment reduction for expected refundable AMIC tax credits.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on 10-Q for CHIPS Act status; Mode B: covenant headroom is conditional on CHIPS award disbursements ($450M trigger reduces minimum-liquidity covenant) — did the awards actually arrive?
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + sec_filings (8-K search for grant announcement)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q (May 2025): Company received $192.1M in cash AMIC tax refunds (refundable federal income-tax credits, not grants) during Q3 FY25. NO confirmation that any CHIPS Act direct capital grants ('award disbursements pursuant to governmental grants') have been received. The $450M-grant covenant trigger that would reduce minimum-liquidity covenant from $750M to $500M had NOT been hit as of the 10-Q filing date. Covenant minimum-liquidity floor stepped UP from $630M to $750M on April 1, 2025 because CHIPS grants did not arrive in time.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The FY24 10-K language was technically honest (it described the CHIPS grant as not-yet-finalized), but the company's capital structure was engineered around the assumption that grants would arrive — and they had not as of the 10-Q. The covenant stepped UP at exactly the moment cash was lowest. Mode B: the absence of a Commerce Dept award announcement 8-K between Aug 2024 and May 2025 is itself a hard counter-signal.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'In fiscal 2024, 2023 and 2022, we had two, two and three customers, respectively, that each represented more than 10% of our consolidated revenue. These customers, in the aggregate, accounted for 37%, 36% and 48%' AND $2.0B Renesas Customer Refundable Deposit Agreement fully received by Q4 FY24.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on 10-Q to identify whether Renesas (the disclosed CRD counterparty) is still ramping as expected; Mode B: customer-concentration risk + the $2.0B Renesas deposits are UNSECURED and refundable, creating contingent liability if Renesas pulls.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q discusses Renesas CRD only as a balance-sheet liability — confirms all $2.0B received and outstanding, but no mention of revenue ramp from the Renesas relationship or any 2025 deposits/amendments. The unsecured-refundable structure means a counterparty dispute or design-in cancellation could create an immediate cash claim against Wolfspeed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K disclosed the structure honestly but did not flag the asymmetry: $2.0B of unsecured customer deposits sit on the balance sheet, the auto SiC market softened in 2024, and the 10-Q does not describe meaningful Renesas-fulfilled revenue. A Renesas refund demand inside the going-concern window would be catastrophic — under-disclosed risk.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'For fiscal 2025, we target approximately $1.2 billion to $1.4 billion of net capital investment' and 'we believe we have the ability to navigate the current environment while maintaining our capital expenditure plans.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on 10-Q to compare actual fiscal-2025 capex run-rate vs guided $1.2-1.4B; Mode B: did capex get cut, signalling distress?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q: '$820.9 million (net of $238.6 million in reimbursements) compared to $1,451.3 million' for the 9 months — i.e. 43% capex reduction YoY. 10-Q describes 'a planned decrease in capital expenditures' and Saarland (Germany) fab disappears from the narrative. Annualized 9-month run-rate (~$1.1B) is at the low end of the $1.2-1.4B target.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capex was being cut materially in 2025 — consistent with cash conservation in distress, inconsistent with the 10-K's confident 'maintaining our capital expenditure plans.' The Germany Saarland fab plan was effectively paused (not mentioned in 10-Q). Strategy walked back without an explicit retraction.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K Item 9A and Note 12 disclose PricewaterhouseCoopers as independent auditor with clean continuing relationship.
rfm_tuples.f: auditor_change_from_text on 10-K + 10-Q + 8-K search for Item 4.01 changes
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: signal=CLEAN_BIG4_TENURE, firms_mentioned=['PricewaterhouseCoopers'], n_resignation_lang=0, n_disagreement_lang=0. No 8-K Item 4.01 in pre-cutoff filings list. Auditor stable.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No auditor-change signal. PwC has not resigned, no disagreement disclosed. This is the one major honest signal on the disclosure-quality axis — they kept their Big-4 auditor through the distress.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied by 10-K: management compensation alignment with shareholders; FY24 10-K filed Aug 22, 2024 with the 'adequate liquidity for 12 months' representation.
rfm_tuples.f: form4 / insider_vs_calendar around capital events (Dec 9 2024 S-3ASR shelf, Oct 22 2024 add-on $250M 2030 Notes); Mode B: did insiders BUY stock to signal confidence, or sell into the distress?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pre-cutoff Form 4 activity Aug 2024 - May 2025: 28 Form 4s, dominated by routine grants. Dec 6 2024 (3 trading days before S-3ASR shelf): cluster of 6 directors each receiving 18,834 RSU grants @ $0 (routine annual board grant timing). NO insider open-market purchases despite stock collapse from ~$15 (Aug 2024) to ~$3 (May 2025). One director (Hodge) SOLD 3,048 shares at $3.28 on May 12, 2025 — 3 days before our cutoff, immediately after the going-concern 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B finding: in a textbook 'management confidence' setup, insiders would buy a distressed stock at $3 to signal conviction in the turnaround. The complete absence of insider purchases plus a director selling 3 days after the going-concern disclosure is a strong negative signal — insiders are not putting money behind the 'we can refinance out-of-court' narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'The Indenture governing the 2030 Senior Notes... includes a liquidity maintenance financial covenant requiring us to have an aggregate amount of unrestricted cash and cash equivalents... of at least $500 million as of the last day of any calendar month, which amount will be reduced over time upon the fulfillment of certain conditions.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on 10-Q to verify whether covenant terms changed (they did) and whether headroom is shrinking
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q reveals covenant is more onerous than the 10-K describes: the floor STEPS UP from $630M to $750M on April 1 2025, only reducing to $500M IF the Company receives $450M of CHIPS grants, and to $250M only if $750M of grants arrive. As of March 30 2025 cash was $1,329.6M against the $750M floor — only $580M of liquidity headroom, before subtracting the $575M 2026 Note maturity and $469M trailing 9-month operating burn.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's representation of the covenant was technically accurate but understated severity — readers of just the 10-K would think the floor was $500M and falling; in reality the floor was stepping UP, and the company was 7-8 months from a covenant breach absent restructuring. The 10-Q makes this explicit; the 10-K obscured it.

rfm_tuples.R: FY24 10-K: 'Design-ins for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024 were $9.1 billion, compared with design-ins of approximately $7.9 billion for the fiscal year ended June 25, 2023. Design-wins for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024 were $5.8 billion, compared with design-wins of $1.8 billion for the fiscal year ended June 25, 2023.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text and claim_evolution: did the 10-Q substantiate the design-in/win pipeline by showing translation into revenue?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-Q: revenue actually DECLINED YoY (Q3 FY25 $185.4M vs Q3 FY24 $200.7M; 9-month $560.6M vs $606.5M). Management acknowledges 'design-wins and design-ins decreased for the nine months ended March 30, 2025' and customers 'ramp at a lower ramp rate than initially expected.' The 10-K's $5.8B design-win figure has not translated to revenue ramp.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic backlog-to-revenue gap. The 10-K's pipeline numbers ($9.1B / $5.8B) were technically truthful per their own definitions ('20% PO of expected first year revenue') but functioned as growth-narrative anchors that the next 9 months of actual revenue did not support. The framework's claim_evolution check catches the divergence between pipeline disclosure and realized revenue.

summary: WOLF's FY24 10-K (filed Aug 2024) was a borderline-honest distress disclosure: it laid out the debt stack ($6.2B), Mohawk Valley underutilization ($124M), Renesas CRD structure, and CHIPS-grant conditionality — but framed liquidity as 'adequate for at least 12 months' and capex as 'maintained.' By the May 9 2025 10-Q (6 days before cutoff), management had explicitly conceded substantial doubt about going concern AND active contemplation of an in-court restructuring with event-of-default consequences. The disclosure delta over 8.6 months reveals the 10-K's confident 12-month liquidity assertion was wrong on its face. Mode B signals reinforce: zero insider purchases through a 5x stock collapse, capex slashed 43%, CHIPS grants undelivered, and the $575M 2026 convertible maturity sitting inside the going-concern horizon with no out-of-court path. The May 2025 10-Q's explicit going-concern + restructuring language is the highest-tier framework signal, captured cleanly pre-cutoff — this is a strong SHORT/AVOID signal that the framework would correctly flag.
